---
name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`, frontend component contracts, or Runtime Client SDK assets. Shared Application Delivery still publishes the Runtime Client SDK for an independent frontend Skill; this Builder Skill never fetches, copies, installs, generates, validates, or takes ownership of it. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. One Host/Agent session and TODO own requirements → model → apply → implementation → verify → package → Runtime → canary → acceptance, including recoverable repair rounds. Follow every applicable routed reference. A light batch may omit only TODO sections allowed by the guide, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |
| complete TODO, Gate first-execution receipts, and session ownership | [session TODO and Gate receipts](references/development-guide.md#session-todo-and-gate-receipts) |
| project ownership and frontend finding routing | [project and frontend boundaries](references/development-guide.md#project-and-frontend-boundaries) |
| requirements extraction and critical ambiguity | [requirements to domain facts](references/development-guide.md#requirements-to-domain-facts) |
| domain truth, settlement, list Report, and technical prevention Gates | [domain truth design](references/development-guide.md#domain-truth-design) |
| capability reconciliation and metadata modeling | [model and capability mapping](references/development-guide.md#model-and-capability-mapping) |
| declarative authoring and the only release command | [model apply is the only release](references/development-guide.md#model-apply-is-the-only-release) |
| bounded installed-batch Action context | [source prepare implementation packet](references/development-guide.md#source-prepare-implementation-packet) |
| valid check, source finalize, focused tests, and exact receipts | [project check to finalize to tests](references/development-guide.md#project-check-to-finalize-to-tests) |
| semantic journey binding and highest-risk canary | [semantic execution and canary](references/development-guide.md#semantic-execution-and-canary) |
| managed Runtime and exact-denominator acceptance | [Runtime and acceptance](references/development-guide.md#runtime-and-acceptance) |
| evidence ceiling and terminal states | [done terminal policy](references/development-guide.md#done-terminal-policy) |
| initial credential and acceptance-identity safety | [system seed login](references/development-guide.md#system-seed-login) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

Before resolving or resuming this continuation, prove the original Host/Agent turn has actually ended. An outer exec session reporting `Unknown process id`, missing its timing trailer, or becoming unreadable is not termination evidence and must never trigger a concurrent Agent against the same session. The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

### Explicit post-apply source-finalization continuation

Use this distinct compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` after a fresh successful `model apply` materialization whose source finalization failed solely on generated project-owned Action placeholders, and the caller has completed those Action sources. It does not accept or alter the already-current `source-finalization-continuation` route.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile post-apply-source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The resolver validates the current signed backend materialization and its exact machine failure receipt before creating state. That receipt must contain only the structured `project.source_placeholder_remains` diagnostics for Action source in the `backend_technical_contract` check; every independent preflight check must have passed, and only the dependent composition check may be skipped. The current source must be a placeholder-free, finalization-ready evolution of that receipt in which only project-owned `backend/actions/**` paths changed. Runtime Client SDK and frontend materialization receipts are never accepted.

On success the resolver atomically owns one TODO, Gate state, and profile with exactly three ordered one-shot recipes:

```text
project check --scope actions → project source finalize → focused Go test
```

Execute only the returned `run_recipes`. Do not edit, add, reorder, duplicate, reopen, attach evidence to, or invoke the underlying product commands outside the profile runner. Partial state, symlinks, traversal or unbounded package paths, changed materialization/failure/source/CLI identities, a forged receipt, any non-placeholder failure, terminal failure, or a different/extra Gate fails closed with no replacement TODO. A completed terminal profile returns no recipes and never reopens. Do **not** read the whole-project guide, TODO template, or another whole-project reference for this profile.

### Explicit project verification continuation

Use this compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-verification-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. It is independent from package continuation. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-verification-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint validates the current backend-only materialization, source finalization and identity, Runtime manifest, and backend Application Delivery binding. Python consumes that checkpoint and atomically owns any required one-Gate TODO/state/profile. If verification is already current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise execute the sole returned machine-owned `project verify --json` recipe exactly once. Never supply a label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or binding. Partial/conflicting/unsafe state, stale profile identity, receipt tampering, an extra or reordered Gate, a repeated terminal command, or a changed pre-execution checkpoint fails closed without replacement.

### Explicit project package continuation

Use this separate compact route only when the caller explicitly requests `project-package-continuation` and thereby accepts and freezes requirements, model, and project source. Do not load the whole-project guide, TODO template, verification authority, production technical Gates, or Gate runner source.

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile project-package-continuation
```

The Go product checkpoint requires the current V6 verification plus the same current backend binding/materialization/finalization/source/Runtime identity closure. If the package receipt is current, the resolver returns terminal completion with no recipe. Otherwise it atomically owns one machine Gate and returns only the fixed `project package --json` recipe. Execute it exactly once; never author its label, kind, Gate ID, argv, or bindings. The same partial, conflict, symlink/traversal, stale/tamper, extra/reordered Gate, terminal-repeat, and pre-execution-change cases fail closed without overwriting state or accepting an older receipt.

### Explicit Runtime process continuation

Use this compact route when the caller asks only to recover the already-packaged managed Runtime start/status boundary. Use the current Host session ID for this fresh compact continuation; do not create or reuse a whole-project TODO for that session. It does not require loading the whole-project guide, verification references, TODO template, verification authorities, or Gate runner source. Resolve the machine-owned profile once:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --profile runtime-process-continuation \
  --runtime-address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
```

When the session has no TODO, Gate state, or Runtime profile, the resolver atomically creates its canonical two-Gate minimal TODO, synchronized state, and profile. It owns the fixed labels, `runtime_start` → `runtime_status` kinds, Gate IDs, exact argv, source/Runtime/cohort bindings, current packaged bundle, packaged CLI, numeric loopback address, and all pinned identities. The tool guarantees that the actual listener is the requested loopback and records its proof; the Agent adds no bind command or listener check. Stdout is only the compact envelope with the remaining `run_recipes`; execute them in order. Do not supply or author a TODO, label, marker, Gate ID, bundle, command argv, or identity binding yourself. Re-resolve after start to obtain only the status recipe when recovering from compaction. A partial session, non-profile-owned TODO, symlink, extra/reordered/forged Gate, changed address/package/source/CLI identity, stale state, terminal failure, or conflict fails closed without deleting or overwriting caller state; a terminal Gate never reopens.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Repair model/input failures and rerun it through a new round-specific Gate in the same session TODO; never reopen a terminal Gate, split release steps, bypass review, or treat `--product-surfaces` as frontend authorization.
- Run each check, finalize, and focused test through its own Gate on first execution. The runner serializes the Gate across processes; a passed or failed receipt makes only that Gate terminal. `checkpoint`, `status`, and `--require-complete` are recovery evidence, not task-exit instructions. After repair, add a round-specific Gate to the same TODO, sync, rerun invalidated checks, and continue in the same Host/Agent session. Never rerun a terminal Gate or reuse another receipt.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- When a settled requirement explicitly names an initial/default field value, add one TODO checkpoint that records the requirement evidence, exact Object-field JSON Pointer, concrete `default_value`, and its matching option/state entry. Close it only after the pointer exists in the applied model and validation proves membership; never leave the behavior only in acceptance prose or infer a default from silence. The authoritative mapping and applied example are in [CRUD and state machine](references/capabilities/crud-and-state-machine.md).
- After finalization and focused tests pass, run the highest-risk semantic canary before broad Runtime integration. Failure makes dependents temporarily ineligible, never ends the task: repair its owner, add repair Gates to the same TODO, rerun invalidated checks, and continue without shrinking the model or denominator.
- Model validation, apply, source checks, verify, package, Runtime start/health, canary, and acceptance failures use the Gate runner's `reconcile --cli "$DOMAINRY_CLI"` contract. `reconcile` never replays a product command: it may migrate only a hash-proven legacy identity or reuse current authoritative receipts, and otherwise returns a typed manual repair queue. Both `done` and recoverable `repair_required` emit complete JSON with exit 0 and `agent_should_stop:false`; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe contract input exits nonzero with `agent_should_stop:true`. Repair the queue in the same TODO/session and invoke it again until `state:"done"`; do not compose a `set -e` attach/run batch.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

item.aggregated_output: # Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. The CLI-compiled capability disclosure and Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source and dependencies stay externally owned and read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [backend-runtime.md](backend-runtime.md) for the closed backend Runtime boundary. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → source implementation → verify → package → managed Runtime → semantic canary → acceptance → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. For normal whole-project work this entire chain, including repair rounds, stays in one Host/Agent session and one TODO. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` and `post-apply-source-finalization-continuation` routes are selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. They never load this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; each compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute first commands through their Gate `run`, then invoke `reconcile --cli "$DOMAINRY_CLI"`. Reconcile never replays product commands; it only validates/migrates exact identities, reuses current authoritative receipts, or queues manual repair. Consume its complete `repair_queue`, repair the typed owner in this session, and invoke it again. Recoverable `repair_required` is continuation JSON with exit 0 and `agent_should_stop:false`; typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe contract input alone exits nonzero and stops. A second reconcile of a current done ledger is a zero-command, zero-mutation no-op; `status --require-complete` remains a read-only checkpoint. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. Normal recovery never changes this identity. A later session exists only after the original task was genuinely interrupted or externally blocked; it creates a new file and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Treat every round as bounded by its complete safely reachable finding inventory, one owner-grouped repair batch, and the invalidated checks it must rerun; repeat while findings remain. Ordinary non-zero results from model validation/apply, source checks, verify, package, Runtime start/health, canary, or acceptance are recoverable inputs to this loop, not an Agent/session boundary. Do not add a compatibility layer, fallback, weaker oracle, excluded case, or reduced denominator. Stop the whole task only after evidence proves one of four genuinely unrecoverable conditions: a required external service, permission, or credential remains unavailable after every authorized recovery path; two or more unresolved business choices would change a required observable result and no accepted authority permits a safe choice; continuation would risk data corruption or security; or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Record the attempted recovery paths and their evidence. Otherwise remain in the same Host/Agent session and TODO, repair, rerun, and continue. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey temporarily ineligible for execution, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner in this session, add any terminal-command repair Gates to the same TODO, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks before automatically continuing. “Blocked” here prevents invalid downstream evidence; it never ends the Agent task. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. This is the authoritative requirements-only routing rule. An item is a `business_blocker` only when accepted evidence leaves at least two concrete, mutually incompatible choices and choosing among them changes a requirement's explicitly demanded observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. # Verification evidence levels

Use this ladder for every verify Gate and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, `project verify`, and packaging pass. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope backend acceptance journey executes end to end on real Runtime data across its complete role/case matrix. Each permission boundary includes allow and deny probes; each data-scope rule uses differentiated identities and records; every mutation includes persistence evidence; Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, and outbox claims include their terminal observable effect.
- `L4_browser_verified`: **outside this Skill's acceptance scope.** The level number is reserved so the ladder stays stable, but browser-layer UI verification is never required, claimed, or a completion precondition here; backend delivery acceptance stops at L3/L5.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `project verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every accepted operation/case row, bind project-local evidence to the current full-stack source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record the operation, actor/role, case, request/response or execution identity, expected owner, permission and data scope, persistence probe, before/after state digest, audit/receipt identity when applicable, and result.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

Whole-project and Runtime-integrated backend completion require current L3 for every in-scope journey and L5 for every critical journey marked restart-sensitive. A light existing-project increment may reference prior current evidence for unchanged operations, but every changed operation and affected regression boundary must reach the same required level. Completion in this Skill is backend acceptance: L3 for every in-scope journey plus L5 for restart-sensitive ones; L4 browser evidence is never required. This Skill never changes frontend source, so it carries no frontend typecheck/build duty; frontend-owned defects are recorded as findings for the frontend owner.
# Verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair.

## Verification closure

After `project verify`, package, and startup of the exact current managed Runtime, run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This creates the CLI-owned `.domainry/builder/acceptance/denominator.json`. Do not edit it. The denominator is generated from requirement IDs, every linked model resource, acceptance scenarios, typed Runtime operations, roles and exact data-scope declarations, plus capability-specific lifecycles. It also contains the mandatory `domainry-semantic-acceptance-contract-v1`: exactly one mapping per denominator case from requirement → actor → formal principal context → fresh setup → command operation → evidence facts → reason-specific oracle. Preparation and every later load fail closed if a mapping is missing or if its actor, command, fact closure, setup isolation, expected outcome/error, or HTTP oracle diverges from the denominator. Its hash binds the current model, Blueprint, capability lock, Runtime Domain API, delivery, Runtime manifest, verification/package receipts, Runtime binary, and stable database cohort identity. The live process PID is intentionally not part of that stable hash because a restart case must replace it; the typed restart artifact must bind the old PID, current new PID, unchanged database cohort, delivery, and binary. A model, capability, source, package, database target, or Runtime change requires a new denominator; `prepare` archives every generation under `.domainry/builder/acceptance/history/denominator/`, and previously recorded results survive an evolution only through the incremental staleness flow below — never by assumption.

The denominator must cover every changed or newly published operation plus referenced prior evidence for unchanged operations. Each case names its Runtime owner, actor/role, permission and data scope, required outcome, error contract, restart sensitivity, and required evidence kinds. Every scoped read and write requires positive and differentiated-scope proof (database-agnostic, by ordinary query/HTTP probes — never engine-level RLS posture; see G14); every protected operation also requires permission-denied proof. Writes additionally require missing-idempotency-key rejection, idempotent replay, idempotency conflict, persistence read-back and audit correlation. Project Actions additionally require one HTTP mutation per business intent, one Runtime unit of work, atomic commit, injected rollback, and concurrency conflict; atomicity is proven by `http_exchange` + `transaction_trace` + `persistence_snapshot` + `audit_correlation`. The denominator never reads frontend source or requires frontend evidence. Each declared Handler Connector call gets its own case bound to the exact connector, connection, provider, operation, execution mode and side-effect class; durable writes require worker restart and terminal reconciliation. Declared notification events require after-commit once-only durable refetch, and every external channel gets its own provider-terminal case. Every Report and typed list/search/query operation requires bounded page and stable traversal cases with a query profile captured on the same database cohort named by the managed process receipt: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, all with statement/row-count observation and machine-checked index/full-scan classification. Evidence whose dialect or plan format differs from `runtime_identity.database_driver` is rejected; no second database or SQLite fallback is allowed. Its signed cursor must either encode the complete deterministic keyset tuple or bind an authorized source version to a bounded offset; a source-version-fenced continuation must reject source drift as a stale-cursor conflict. Automation Rules derive before-transaction rollback or after-commit restart/terminal cases from their trigger. Agent resources additionally require task cancel/retry/reconcile with terminal worker/audit evidence and interactive SSE disconnect/resume. A manual approval Workflow is proven as a durable process: start before the managed Runtime replacement, refetch after restart, decide real assigned tasks through participant APIs, and observe terminal persistence/audit; it does not claim `worker_terminal` unless the graph actually schedules worker-owned work. Scheduled jobs and governed report exports retain worker restart/resume evidence. Typed operations declared by acceptance `config.runtime_operations` must resolve to the pinned Runtime API and include both positive and denied rows for writes. Read and apply all 32 families in [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md); a project may mark a family not applicable only from model-derived evidence.

Semantic oracles are strict. Each scenario uses fresh setup identities/records or names an explicit dependency whose passing evidence is current. A positive case must identify and observe its intended target with the required non-empty facts; a `2xx` paired with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or different record is not proof unless that exact value is the confirmed outcome. A negative case must reach the intended stable status/error/concealment and prove unchanged durable state; an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, empty result caused by bad setup, or exception from a missing dependency is not the expected rejection. Scope isolation probes use otherwise equivalent requests against the same target through formal matching and non-matching Runtime sessions, plus the broader in-scope role when applicable. Runtime-owned identity/context values in setup and requests must come from the formal typed client, seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and be carried unchanged; synthetic claims or hand-normalized canonical values invalidate the case.

### Runner-first acceptance execution

With the denominator prepared and the managed Runtime healthy, execute the mechanical case families through the platform runner FIRST — before writing any harness code:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The runner (capability `project.acceptance.run`, diagnostic report contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-run-v2`) mechanically executes the standard Action, Automation, Report GET-summary, Runtime read-route, Workflow, governed export and Scheduler families against the live Runtime and the exact sqlite/mysql/postgres database cohort bound by its managed process receipt, validates every artifact with the same `acceptance check` validators before writing it, and atomically writes/merges one complete `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2` document. External cohorts require the same explicit `DATABASE_DRIVER`/`DATABASE_DSN` environment binding already used by the managed Runtime; the runner compares only non-secret DSN/cohort identities and never serializes the DSN. It contains exactly one row per denominator case: `passed`, `declared_gap`, or `not_passed` with typed responsibility. Existing passed/gap rows are immutable; existing `not_passed` rows are retried. The separate `.domainry/development/acceptance-evidence/backend-acceptance-run.json` is execution diagnostics, not a second source of case truth. For every case the runner uses the semantic contract's exact actor and calls the authenticated Runtime `GET /identity/principal-context` resolver; Runtime returns canonical workspace/workforce/organization/business-profile/surface selectors, and the runner carries only those selectors into requests. Neither runner nor business harness may infer a user from role ordering, construct profile headers, or query Runtime-owned identity tables. Never re-implement or overwrite a runner-passed case. A `not_passed` outcome with `disposition:"runtime_failed"` is an observed contract violation — a product defect to repair at its owner, never a harness problem. Only `needs_business_harness` rows belong in the self-built harness. `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, and `runtime_failed` return to their named owner first; downstream cases sharing a failed setup are `blocked_dependency`, not independent failures.

Self-built harness code must be a thin assertion layer on top of [acceptance-harness-core.py](../assets/acceptance-harness-core.py): copy that file unchanged into `.domainry/development/`, then write only per-case assertion functions against it — never re-implement session/auth bootstrap, HTTP or database capture, artifact/evidence/results writers, resume state, retry/backoff plumbing, or any DSN parser/adapter. SQLite is stdlib-backed. For MySQL, install `PyMySQL` in the harness environment and call `AcceptanceDatabase.from_runtime_state(PROJECT_ROOT, state)` (or construct `Harness` normally) with no callback: core lazy-loads PyMySQL and exclusively accepts the managed Runtime Go-style contract `user:<password>@tcp(host:port)/database?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local`. URL DSNs, omitted or invalid targets/ports, and added, reordered, unknown, or dangerous query semantics fail closed; the password may be empty and is never emitted. Agent-written MySQL connectors and DSN parsers are prohibited. PostgreSQL retains the explicit advanced DB-API 2 `database_connector(driver, dsn, schema)` boundary. For both external drivers, core reads the random in-database marker and derives `sha256("domainry-managed-runtime-database-cohort-v1\n" + driver + "\n" + receipt.database_dsn_identity_sha256 + "\n" + marker_identity)` before comparing it with the managed Runtime receipt's `database_identity_sha256`; the marker is never itself the receipt identity, and copied marker rows at a different DSN identity fail closed. Missing or invalid receipt/marker contracts and identities are rejected without fallback. Core suppresses connector stdout/stderr, owns dialect SQL/EXPLAIN and DSN/password redaction, and never falls back to SQLite. Use `harness.session_for_case(case)` exclusively for the frozen actor/principal mapping. Register cases in `ScenarioGraph`; each setup receives a fresh opaque namespace, `setup_failed` is distinct from a product failure, and downstream cases become `blocked_dependency` rather than executing against missing residue. Apply `ReasonOracle` for exact positive, rejection, state, scope, and audit assertions before sealing evidence.

Execute only the remaining `needs_business_harness` cases through that real acceptance harness and project-provisioned non-human Runtime identities. The harness—not prose editing—writes typed HTTP exchanges, SSE transcripts, durable refetches, idempotency receipts, database snapshots, transaction and pagination traces, query profiles, audit correlation, differentiated-scope data, provider receipts, worker terminal observations, and restart observations under project-owned `backend/tests/evidence/**`. Self-built harness code and every intermediate working file live under `.domainry/development/**` from the very first file, never anywhere under `backend/**`: harness files inside `backend/**` dirty the finalized `source_sha256` and make every gate receipt stale, and the measured cost of that mistake is a full finalize/verify/package redo plus re-recording all evidence. Every structured observation references one real regular non-symlink artifact and its SHA-256; persistence evidence also supplies before/after hashes and, for replay, the replay hash. Results and every evidence document bind the denominator and Runtime identity hashes. Then run:

The result document contract is `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2`: copy `denominator_sha256`, `runtime_identity`, and `runtime_identity_sha256` exactly from the denominator and provide exactly one `results[]` row for every denominator case. A `passed` row contains `case_id`, `state`, and `evidence[]` (`path`, `sha256`); a `not_passed` row contains no evidence and requires `outcome.disposition`, stable `code`, `owner`, `root_case_id`, `retryable`, and factual `reason`; a `declared_gap` row uses the existing typed gap contract. `acceptance check` fails closed while any `not_passed` row remains. The business harness may replace only a row whose disposition is `needs_business_harness`; it cannot replace platform, dependency, setup, evidence, unsupported-runner, or Runtime failures. Each referenced evidence document is `domainry-backend-acceptance-evidence-v1` with `state:"passed"`, the exact case/denominator/Runtime hashes, and `observations[]`. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. `reconcile` never replays a product command and never overwrites a stale declared pass with a failed attempt: a strictly verifiable legacy cohort may receive an explicit migration receipt, a prior pass may be restored only from intact authoritative evidence, and every other case enters the typed manual repair queue. Recoverable `repair_required` exits 0 for shell continuation; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe input exits nonzero. Then repair the named owner, create new round-specific Gates for invalidated commands, and continue; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly. Treat every `failed` row as one repair inventory and never treat `skipped_dependency` as a pass. These receipts remain L1 structural evidence only.

Run and bind evidence for:

- protected source boundary (`frontend/**` untouched under every recorded frontend mutation scope — no frontend typecheck/test/build set exists in this Skill because it never changes frontend source), and current source finalization;
- backend format, lint, vet, focused tests, full tests, verification, and package receipts;
- exact Runtime delivery/manifest identity and healthy managed Runtime;
- real non-human acceptance sessions and differentiated seed data;
- the complete operation x role x required-case inventory;

- Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, outbox, and external-effect terminal outcomes;
